changes.summary: Inspired by a trip to Europe in the early 1950s, industrialist and future governor of Puerto Rico Luis A. Ferré founded the Museo de Arte de Ponce in 1958 and, over the next decade, assembled a remarkable collection of European and American paintings spanning historical periods and geographic regions for his fellow citizens. The museum’s collection of contemporary Puerto Rican paintings grew soon after, embedding works by local artists within broader traditions and highlighting Puerto Rican cultural identity. Sense of Beauty features 60 paintings on loan from the Museo de Arte de Ponce that span a range of styles and genres—history painting, religious art, genre painting, landscape, and portraiture. Works by key European and American painters from the 1520s to the 1920s are placed in dialogue with twentieth- and twenty-first-century Puerto Rican artists whose works shed new light on the European canon. A shared aesthetic quality unites these paintings: a sense of beauty that evolved over half a millennium. The traveling exhibition allows the Museo de Arte de Ponce to undergo renovations to repair damage caused by major earthquakes in 2020. We look forward to visitors experiencing the immersive beauty of these works, carrying forward Ferré’s belief that art should play a significant role in the lives of all people and our shared mission to make it accessible to all.
